about.name: Tracey Sun
about.title: Architect & Designer
about.subtitle: M.Arch Candidate, Columbia University GSAPP
about.bio: I am a Masters of Architecture candidate at Columbia University's Graduate School of Architecture, Planning and Preservation. My work explores the intersection of structure, materiality, and lived experience — using line, light, and space as primary instruments of design.
about.bio2: Drawing from both computational and hand-drafted traditions, I pursue architecture that is precise yet humane, rigorous yet poetic. My portfolio spans urban housing, cultural institutions, and speculative research into the future of the built environment.

projects.title: Threshold
projects.description: An adaptive reuse and infill housing project in Harlem that rethinks the threshold between public street and private dwelling. The project introduces a series of transitional spaces — stoops, light courts, and shared gardens — that mediate between urban density and domestic intimacy.

projects.title: Strata
projects.description: A geology museum embedded into a hillside along the Hudson River. The building is organized around a continuous sectional cut that reveals geological layers, making the ground itself the primary exhibit. Concrete, glass, and corten steel trace the stratigraphy of the site.

projects.title: Lattice
projects.description: A computational study of structural lattice systems derived from crystallographic geometry. The research investigates how non-repeating tiling patterns — Penrose and Ammann–Beenker — can generate structurally efficient and spatially rich enclosures for large-span public buildings.

projects.title: Fold
projects.description: A site-specific paper installation exploring the structural logic of origami at architectural scale. Folded Kraft paper panels span a 12-meter bay, achieving rigidity through geometry alone. The work questions how material intelligence embedded in folding can inform tectonic thinking.

projects.title: Commons
projects.description: A proposal for a new civic commons in Brownsville, Brooklyn, anchored by a community library, a market hall, and a series of flexible outdoor rooms. The design draws on the morphology of the historic New York street grid while reinterpreting it for contemporary community life.

projects.title: Grain
projects.description: A series of hand-crafted furniture objects exploring the expressive potential of wood grain. Each piece is designed to expose and celebrate the natural patterning of the material — knots, rays, and annual rings — as primary ornament. Joinery is left visible as structural honesty.
